drawer.title: GEO readiness
drawer.subtitle: Can AI crawlers actually read this page?

verdict.ok: Every crawler we tested can read this page.
verdict.thin: Some crawlers receive far less text than a browser. The page may need JavaScript to show its content.
verdict.unpublished: This page has never been published, so there is no public URL to test yet.
verdict.empty: Even a browser receives almost no text before JavaScript runs ({{count}} words). Crawlers will see an empty page.

crawler.initialHtml: What the crawler receives before JavaScript runs

explain.403: The server refused this crawler. This is usually a firewall or bot-protection rule, not a content problem.
explain.jsOnly: A browser sees much more text than the crawler does. The content probably arrives through JavaScript, which crawlers do not run.
explain.empty: The initial HTML is a shell. The content arrives through JavaScript, or after a client-side redirect, and crawlers do not run either. Server-side rendering is the fix, not a robots.txt change.
explain.blockedButAllowed: Your robots.txt allows {{count}} of these crawlers, but the server refused them anyway. The block is coming from a firewall or bot protection, not from your content or your robots.txt. This is an infrastructure fix.
explain.reachableButDisallowed: Your robots.txt tells {{count}} of these crawlers not to fetch this page. They can reach it, but a well-behaved crawler will not read it. Change robots.txt if you want them to.

crawler.metaRefresh: Client-side redirect: the page tells a browser to go to {{url}}. Crawlers stay on this shell.

error.generic: The check could not be completed.
error.rateLimit: Too many checks in a short time. Try again in a few minutes.
error.notPublished: Publish this page first, then run the check.

robots.title: robots.txt
robots.absent: This site has no robots.txt. Every crawler is allowed everywhere by default. That works, but nobody decided it.
robots.noneNamed: No AI crawler is named in robots.txt. They all fall under the wildcard rule, so they are allowed by default rather than on purpose.
robots.someNamed: {{count}} AI crawler is named explicitly in robots.txt.
robots.someNamed_plural: {{count}} AI crawlers are named explicitly in robots.txt.
robots.someDisallowed: {{count}} of them cannot fetch this page.

control.title: Control AI crawlers
control.intro: Sets each crawler's site-wide stance in robots.txt. Groups you have not changed are left exactly as they are, comments and Sitemap lines included.
control.applied: Written and published. Run the check again to see it.
control.cannotWrite: You do not have permission to change this site's settings.
control.noMixin: This site has no robots.txt yet. Applying will create one.
control.placeholder: What is stored is the module's placeholder, not a real file.
control.error: robots.txt could not be read or written.
control.rule: Blocking replaces that crawler's rules with a site-wide refusal. Allowing only undoes a site-wide refusal: a crawler with path rules such as Disallow: /docs/ is left alone, because flattening that would throw away work. A crawler sharing a group with others is moved into its own group so the others keep their rules.

llms.title: llms.txt
llms.absent: No llms.txt at the site root (HTTP {{status}}). AI engines have no curated map of your best content.
llms.servedHtml: The site returned an HTML page for /llms.txt instead of a text file. That counts as not having one.

generate.title: Generate from the page tree
generate.intro: Builds the file from published pages, their titles and their descriptions. No model, no external service: the same site always produces the same file.
generate.unchanged: Identical to what is already stored. Nothing to apply.
generate.differs: This differs from what is stored. Review it before applying.
generate.placeholder: What is stored is the module's placeholder, not a real file.
generate.noMixin: The site has no llms.txt yet. Applying will create one.
generate.cannotWrite: You do not have permission to change this site's settings.
generate.applied: Written and published. Run the check again to see it.
generate.rule: Pages hidden from the navigation are left out, and descriptions are never invented. Edit the text before applying if you want something different: what you see is exactly what gets written.

files.editedInSettings: robots.txt and llms.txt belong to the whole site. Edit them under Additional, SEO, GEO readiness.

score.headline: {{passed}} of {{total}} checks passed
score.allGood: Everything we can check from here passes.
score.rubric: Each check reads one fact already in this report. Being disallowed in robots.txt is not counted as a failure: refusing a crawler is a legitimate choice. A disagreement between the policy and the server is.

reachable.label: Every AI crawler gets the page
reachable.fix: At least one crawler was refused. That is usually a firewall or bot-protection rule rather than a content problem.

policyMatchesReality.label: robots.txt matches what the server does
policyMatchesReality.fix: The policy and the server disagree for at least one crawler. One of the two is wrong, and the report names which.

noClientRedirect.label: No client-side redirect
noClientRedirect.fix: The page tells a browser to go elsewhere. Crawlers do not follow that, so this shell is all they read.

namedInRobots.label: AI crawlers named in robots.txt
namedInRobots.fix: No AI crawler is named. They fall to the wildcard group, so you have no explicit policy for them.

contentInInitialHtml.label: Real text in the initial HTML
contentInInitialHtml.fix: The page returns almost no text before JavaScript runs. Server-side rendering is the fix, not a robots.txt change.

sameContentForCrawlers.label: Crawlers get the same text as a browser
sameContentForCrawlers.fix: At least one crawler receives far less text than the browser did. Check what the server varies on the user agent.

title.label: Title present and a usable length
title.fix: A title under 10 or over 70 characters is either uninformative or truncated wherever it is quoted.

singleH1.label: Exactly one H1
singleH1.fix: Zero or several H1 headings leave the main subject of the page ambiguous.

headingOutline.label: Sub-headings structure the page
headingOutline.fix: Retrieval splits pages on headings. A page with no H2 is one undifferentiated block.

metaDescription.label: Meta description present
metaDescription.fix: Without it the summary shown alongside an answer is generated from whatever text comes first.

canonical.label: Canonical URL declared
canonical.fix: Without a canonical, the same content reachable at several addresses is treated as several pages.

langDeclared.label: Page language declared
langDeclared.fix: The html lang attribute is missing, so the language has to be guessed. On a multilingual site that is a real risk.

structuredData.label: Structured data present
structuredData.fix: No JSON-LD was found. Schema types are the most direct way to state what this page is about.

freshness.label: Modification date published
freshness.fix: No dateModified was found. Assistants weigh recency, and an undated page cannot show it is current.

imageAlt.label: Images carry alt text
imageAlt.fix: Some images have no alt text. To a text-only crawler those images simply do not exist.

robotsPresent.label: robots.txt is served
robotsPresent.fix: No robots.txt. Everything is allowed by default, which is a decision you did not get to make.

llmsPresent.label: llms.txt is served
llmsPresent.fix: No llms.txt. It is the one file that tells an assistant which pages matter and why.

diff.identical: No change. The file would be written exactly as it is now.

dashboard.title: GEO readiness for site {{site}} - {{language}}
dashboard.intro: The two files that tell AI crawlers what to do with this site: robots.txt states the policy, llms.txt says which pages matter and why. Both belong to the whole site, so they are edited here rather than from a page.
